verses.text: He said to Moses, “Come up to Yahweh, you, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship from a distance.
Moses alone shall come near to Yahweh, but they shall not come near. The people shall not go up with him.”
Moses came and told the people all Yahweh’s words, and all the ordinances; and all the people answered with one voice, and said, “All the words which Yahweh has spoken will we do.”
Moses wrote all Yahweh’s words, and rose up early in the morning, and built an altar under the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent young men of the children of Israel, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of cattle to Yahweh.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people, and they said, “All that Yahweh has spoken will we do, and be obedient.”
Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.”
Then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up.
They saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was like a paved work of sapphire  stone, like the skies for clearness.
He didn’t lay his hand on the nobles of the children of Israel. They saw God, and ate and drank.
Yahweh said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain, and stay here, and I will give you the stone tablets with the law and the commands that I have written, that you may teach them.”
Moses rose up with Joshua, his servant, and Moses went up onto God’s Mountain.
He said to the elders, “Wait here for us, until we come again to you. Behold, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever is involved in a dispute can go to them.”
Moses went up on the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
Yahweh’s glory settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. The seventh day he called to Moses out of the middle of the cloud.
The appearance of Yahweh’s glory was like devouring fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel.
Moses entered into the middle of the cloud, and went up on the mountain; and Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

footnotes.content: The call echoes up the mountain—Moses, Aaron, and the elders are invited into God's presence. Notice the order: the people stay below, worship from a distance, while the leaders climb higher. Even in closeness to the Lord, there are thresholds we respect.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses alone draws nearest. In those shadows—between the elders and the cloud—we see a pattern: God works through one servant at a time, stepping closer into mystery. The people watch from below, and that too is a calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One voice: "All that Yahweh has spoken will we do." A covenant is not hidden counsel—it is spoken aloud, heard together, answered with unity. The people speak their commitment plainly before the Lord hears it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses writes down Yahweh's words first—a scribe before an architect. Then twelve pillars for twelve tribes, built at dawn when the mind is clear and the mountain is still. The covenant is both written and embodied in stone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Young men offer the burnt offerings—the smoke rises before the people's promise is sealed. These are not the elders, but the young whose hands are strong and whose future depends on the covenant keeping.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Half the blood goes to the basin; half to the altar. This ancient practice—the blood divided between vessel and place—speaks of connection: the people bound together in the middle, the Lord's presence witnessed at the center.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses reads the book aloud—every word heard by all ears. Then the people answer again: "We will do and be obedient." Hearing and answering, not once but twice, shows the seriousness of what binds them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "This is the blood of the covenant." The blood is sprinkled on the people now—it marks them. In later days, readers would see in this moment an echo of another covenant sealed in blood, more perfect and eternal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They go up together—Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the elders. A company climbing toward the holy mountain. The ascent itself is part of the covenant—these feet, these eyes, stepping into the revealed presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Under his feet, a sapphire pavement—as if heaven itself has a foundation that shines. They see the God of Israel, not hidden but manifest, and the vision is clear as sky. Glory fills the mountain where they stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God does not lay his hand on them in judgment—and so they eat and drink. This is intimacy: to see the Holy One face-to-face and live, then to share a meal together as covenant partners. Grace holds the moment in peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Come up higher still, Moses is told. Stone tablets with the law written by Yahweh's own hand—not carved later, but already complete. Moses will teach them, but the Lord is the real author of what binds them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua the servant goes with Moses—one who will later lead the people into promised land, now climbing toward the cloud. Even in these quieter verses, God prepares the next servant, the next generation, for their own callings.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron and Hur remain with the elders—given a quiet station of faithfulness. Not every calling is to climb the mountain. Some are called to hold steady in the valley, judges of disputes, keepers of order until Moses returns.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cloud covers the mountain now, a sign that Moses has entered Yahweh's house. Below, the people see the summit veiled—reminder that God's presence is both revealed and hidden, known and mysterious.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six days the glory settles, and on the seventh, Yahweh calls from within the cloud. Even time obeys him—the pattern of work and rest reflected in when he speaks. Moses hears the voice, patient in the waiting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Devouring fire—the glory of Yahweh unmistakable from the valley. The people see it and know: what we have bound ourselves to is real, alive, consuming. Not a distant idea but presence that burns on the mountain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty days and forty nights—a long keeping in the cloud, hidden from sight. Readers today hear an echo in that wilderness time: a number God repeats when making or testing his servants. In our own dark nights of waiting, that number reminds us: the Lord knows his timetable, and always emerges.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
